clue.text: Hit extremely elegant golf shot

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the next word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: to sock someone is to punch them
the two end letters of elegant

explanation.surface: A golfer strikes the ball with a perfect, stylish shot.
explanation.walkthrough: SOCK + ET. 'Hit' looks like part of the golf picture but is the first piece; a socket is the golfer's dreaded shank off the hosel.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a socket is a shank, a mishit struck off the neck of the club that squirts sideways.

clue.text: "Second-class" not in new Chambers English, I've no idea why

indicators.note: not in says the letter for second-class is absent from the dictionary name
new means made afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B is the grade below A, second class
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs at why 'second-class' is missing from the latest Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMBERS minus B, plus E, rearranged. Chambers is the British dictionary crossword setters favour.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Search me' is an idiom said with a shrug, meaning the speaker has no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Attack head of Royal Horse

indicators.note: head of picks out only the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to charge is to rush forward in attack
the first letter of Royal

explanation.surface: The Royal Horse Guards launch an assault, led by their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARGE + R. 'Royal Horse' reads as one regiment, but horse alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a horse trained for battle or parade, the mount of a knight or cavalry officer.

clue.text: Worn out former partner detested touring America

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the hate word goes around America's letters

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover
a direct synonym
the United States

explanation.surface: A tired former spouse loathed travelling around the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + HA(US)TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted means completely tired out, drained of all energy.

clue.text: Product designed for musical that's likely to fold?

definitions.text: Product designed for musical that's likely to fold?

blocks.clueFragment: Product designed for musical that's likely to fold?
blocks.note: surface reading: merchandise for a stage show that is expected to close quickly
setter's reading: headwear for a night at a musical performance, built to collapse flat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' suggests a flop closing early; here it means collapsing flat. 'Musical' stands for the opera, and the item is a collapsible top hat worn there.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat, sprung so it can be flattened and kept under the theatre seat.

clue.text: How to see Goa, cheaply, flying with a kid?

definitions.text: How to see Goa, cheaply, flying with a kid?

indicators.note: flying means scattered through the air, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent asks how to fly to Goa on a budget with a child in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the fodder overlap: 'Goa, cheaply' is both the description and part of the letters. Goa is a beach state in India popular with tour operators.
explanation.definitionFit: A package holiday bundles flights and hotel at one low price, a budget way to visit a resort.

clue.text: Opponent runs one opener out in Test ground

indicators.note: opener out says the first letter of the ground's name is dropped

blocks.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one
the Oval is a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches

explanation.surface: The other side scores runs while one opening batsman is dismissed at a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: R + I + OVAL minus its first letter. A Test is an international cricket match, and THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival is someone competing against you, an opponent.

clue.text: Husband, timeless Prince Consort, beginning to draw weapon

indicators.note: timeless means without the letter for time, which comes out of the consort's name
beginning to picks just the first letter of the following word

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband, was the Prince Consort
the first letter of draw

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's husband, the eternal Prince Consort, starts to unsheathe a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: H + ALBERT minus T + D.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a medieval pole weapon combining an axe blade and a spike.

clue.text: Warm, delicious sandwiches back in igloo

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between two slices, so the tasty word goes around a letter
back in means the last letter, at the back of the word

blocks.note: a direct synonym
the final letter of igloo

explanation.surface: Delicious warm sandwiches are served inside an igloo.
explanation.walkthrough: T(O)ASTY. 'Sandwiches' looks like food in the scene; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for comfortably warm, as if just out of the toaster.

clue.text: King Herod: repugnant, revolting

indicators.note: revolting means rising up and overturning order, so the letters are overturned

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: King Herod is called disgusting and loathsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Herod' reads as one name, but King alone is the definition and Herod joins repugnant as fodder; 'revolting' then seems a third insult but is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uther Pendragon was the legendary British king of Arthurian story, father of King Arthur.

clue.text: Dad's back, he's in an upstairs room having lost interest

indicators.note: back means the word for Dad is read from its end towards its start
in says one word sits inside the room named after it

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
taken as written
the attic is the room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: Father has returned and is sulking upstairs in the attic, bored with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: AP + AT(HE)TIC. The apostrophes are just joins: 'Dad's back' is Dad is back, and 'he's in' is he is in.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest or enthusiasm, the state of someone who has stopped caring.

clue.text: Team having a way to contain Liverpool's wingers

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the two outside letters of the city are wanted
to contain says the route word wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: via means by way of, and is also a Roman road
the first and last letters of Liverpool

explanation.surface: A football side finds a way to stop Liverpool's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: VI(LL)A. The team is Aston Villa, an English Premier League football club, usually called just Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Villa is the everyday short name of Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club.

clue.text: Oxford University student wearing prison clothing

indicators.note: whatever is wearing something has it around it, so the prison wraps around the student letters

blocks.note: the initials of Oxford University
L is the learner plate, a crossword student
a cage is a place of confinement

explanation.surface: An Oxford undergraduate is locked up and dressed in a convict's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison clothing' reads as one phrase, but it splits: prison is wordplay, and clothing alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a light hooded waterproof jacket, an item of outdoor wear.

clue.text: Complaint from the German pulled out of train crash

indicators.note: pulled out of says some letters are removed from the longer word that follows

blocks.note: a train crash in which the train leaves the rails
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A grievance about a German who was dragged from a wrecked train.
explanation.walkthrough: The train crash must first be turned into its own single word before the German article comes off its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness, which is what an ailment is.

clue.text: 1,000 become weary going over desert

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the word for growing weary is read backwards

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A thousand travellers grow tired while crossing a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: M + TIRE reversed. 'Desert' is not sand here: it is the noun in 'just deserts', what someone deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert, as in getting one's just deserts, is what one deserves, which is one's worth or merit.

clue.text: Rule out report that this puzzle was written in advance?

indicators.note: a report is something said and heard, so the spoken form counts, not the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: this puzzle was written in advance
blocks.note: a crossword prepared beforehand has had its clues written early

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether this crossword's clues were all set long before publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's joke: a puzzle written ahead would be 'pre-clued', which is said like the word meaning to prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it or make it impossible, so to rule it out.

clue.text: They're supporters of light, by the way?

definitions.text: They're supporters of light, by the way?

blocks.note: surface reading: fans or advocates of illumination, perhaps spiritual light
setter's reading: the things standing beside the road that hold up street lights

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' is the casual aside, but here it means literally beside the road; supporters are physical props.
explanation.definitionFit: Street posts carrying lamps line the roadside, physically holding the lights up.

clue.text: County Day to include a hot drink as support for the weary

indicators.note: to include says the county and day letters wrap around the drink

blocks.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county
tea is the classic hot drink
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A county holds a day offering hot drinks to tired visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county north of London, routinely shortened in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, which holds up a tired sleeper.

clue.text: Cool party in which naked gangs dance

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go
in which says the party word holds the next letters inside it

blocks.note: a fan is a device that cools
a do is a party
gangs with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: At a hip party, unclothed gangs take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: FAN + D(ANG)O. 'Cool' looks like an adjective for the party; it is a noun giving the device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, danced by a couple.

clue.text: Plug commercial interest rate bearing note

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the interest rate letters carry the musical note inside them

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
APR is the annual percentage rate quoted on loans
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A product placement in an advert about loan interest rates carries a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: The sol-fa note settles the spelling: TE gives the -ER form, where the alternative spelling of the device would need a different ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a plug fitting that lets a device connect to a socket of a different type.

clue.text: Second very large European elk

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A huge European deer is described in a nature guide.
explanation.walkthrough: MO + OS + E. OS for outsize is a crossword staple from clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Europe the animal Americans call a moose is known as an elk; they are the same species.

clue.text: Exposed firm voided mediocre result

indicators.note: voided means emptied, so the inner letters go and only the ends stay

blocks.note: out means revealed, as a secret is out
Co is the abbreviation for company
mediocre emptied of its middle

explanation.surface: A company caught out produces an average set of results.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT + CO + ME. 'Voided' could apply to firm, but CO is the short form, and mediocre is the word emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the way something turns out, its result.

clue.text: Nietzsche maliciously conceals plan

indicators.note: conceals says the answer lies tucked inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: The philosopher Nietzsche spitefully hides his intentions.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHEME also hides in Nietzsche, but the next letter is A, not E.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan of something.

clue.text: Sounds like hard work, Sir Geoffrey!

indicators.note: sounds like asks for a word said the same as the phrase that follows

blocks.note: a chore is a hard or tedious task, then the polite address

explanation.surface: Someone groans to a knight named Geoffrey that a job is tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir Geoffrey' suggests the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott, but the Sir belongs to the spoken phrase, leaving Geoffrey to name the medieval poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Chaucer, author of The Canterbury Tales, is the best-known poet of that first name.

clue.text: Washington upset Catholic Church when wiping electronic disc

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the capital's letters run the other way
wiping means erasing, so the electronic letter is removed from the church

blocks.note: Washington DC, the District of Columbia
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Washington is angered when the Catholic Church erases a digital disc.
explanation.walkthrough: DC reversed + ROME minus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A CD-ROM is a compact disc holding read-only computer data.

clue.text: Momentum politician sitting in suite, relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters of the suite are loosened and rearranged
sitting in says the politician is placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Momentum activist lounges comfortably in a hotel suite.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is also the name of a left-wing British political group, which makes the politician look natural in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force that keeps something moving, its driving momentum.

clue.text: Record time claimed by retired Frenchman

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the Frenchman's name is read backwards
claimed by says the time is taken inside the name

blocks.note: René is a typical French man's name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A record time is set by a Frenchman who has now stopped competing.
explanation.walkthrough: RENE reversed around T. 'Record time' reads as one phrase; split it, and record is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, writing it into a register or log.

clue.text: PM lets go and goes crazy

indicators.note: something gone crazy is wildly disordered, so the preceding letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister cracks under pressure, gives up and loses his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes crazy' looks like the definition; it is the signal, and the short PM is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was four times Prime Minister of Britain under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Herb tea, grim on yucky cups

indicators.note: cups means holds within, so the run of letters sits inside the phrase before it

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A herbal tea tastes so grim and nasty that it fills the cups.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb tea in the surface is a decoy: tea starts the run of letters rather than being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered plant of the rose family, long used in herbal remedies.

clue.text: Climb Andes shivering, penetrated by cold

indicators.note: shivering means trembling and jumbled, so the mountains' letters are disordered
penetrated by says the cold letter goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Mountaineers shiver as they scale the Andes in bitter cold.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into a rearrangement of ANDES; with only one letter added, the order of the two steps does not change the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend a mountain is to climb it, going upwards.
